items.description: Run two independent AI reviewers that must both approve before any user-facing output, code, or content is published or deployed.
items.summary: The santa-method skill implements multi-agent adversarial verification with a convergence loop. A generator produces the artifact, then two independent reviewers with no shared context evaluate the same rubric in parallel. Both must pass before output ships; otherwise a fix cycle collects all flags, repairs issues, and re-runs dual review until convergence or escalation. Use before public deploy, compliance-sensitive releases, customer-facing copy, or high hallucination-risk content where single-reviewer bias is unacceptable. Do not use for internal drafts or tasks already covered by build, test, and lint pipelines. Architecture phases are generate, dual independent review, verdict gate, and fix cycle with a configurable maximum iteration count. Reviewers return structured pass or fail per rubric criterion with cited issues rather than prose summaries. The method targets outputs where accuracy, brand constraints, or regulatory language require independent double-checking rather than spot review alone.

items.summary: System Design is an agent skill presenting a structured framework for large-scale distributed architecture and interview-style designs. A 0-10 scoring rubric expects stated requirements, estimates, building blocks, scaling, reliability, and acknowledged compromises. Reliability covers health checks, observability pillars, blue-green and canary deploys, RPO and RTO, and autoscaling signals.

items.summary: Negotiation is an agent skill teaching Chris Voss FBI hostage-negotiation tactics for salary, contract, vendor, and high-stakes conversations. Core principle: people want to feel understood and safe, so empathy and listening beat argument and compromise splitting. The skill scores preparation 0-10 against eight frameworks. Tactical empathy vocalizes the counterpart perspective before stating your position. Mirroring repeats the last one to three critical words with silence to prompt elaboration. Labeling names emotions with It seems like phrasing to diffuse negatives. Calibrated questions use How and What instead of accusatory Why, including How am I supposed to do that for price pushback. Accusation audits preempt negatives early. That is right summaries aim for genuine understanding, distinct from dismissive You are right. Ackerman bargaining sequences offers at 65, 85, 95, and 100 percent of target with precise final numbers plus a non-monetary bonus. Black Swan discovery hunts hidden constraints or motivations. Diagnostics cover BATNA, counterpart styles, and voice delivery including late-night DJ tone after key statements.
highlights: Eight frameworks: tactical empathy, mirroring, labeling, calibrated questions, accusation audit, That's right, Ackerman,
Ackerman method sequences 65-85-95-100 percent offers with precise final numbers and a non-monetary sweetener.
Accusation audit lists negatives the counterpart may think and addresses them before objections surface.

items.name: address-sanitizer
items.author: trailofbits
items.description: Automatically detect memory corruption bugs that arise from unsafe address handling in compiled code.
items.summary: AddressSanitizer (ASan) is a compile-time memory error detection tool that instruments C/C++ binaries to catch buffer overflows, use-after-free, double-free, and memory leak bugs during fuzzing and testing. Developers enable it via the `-fsanitize=address` compiler flag and configure behavior with `ASAN_OPTIONS` environment variables. ASan maps virtual memory to track allocation state, delivering detailed error reports with stack traces and allocation/deallocation context. It integrates with libFuzzer, AFL++, cargo-fuzz, and honggfuzz; however, it incurs 2-4x performance overhead and requires unlimited memory limits (`-rss_limit_mb=0` or `-m none`). Best suited for C/C++ and Rust unsafe code testing; skip for production deployments and safe-language-only projects. Compile with `-fsanitize=address -g` flag to instrument memory operations and track allocations. Detects buffer overflows, use-after-free, double-free, and memory leaks at runtime. Requires disabling fuzzer memory limits (`-rss_limit_mb=0` libFuzzer, `-m none` AFL++) due to 20TB virtual memory mapping.

items.name: constant-time-testing

items.description: Detect timing side channels in cryptographic implementations before they reach production.
items.summary: Constant-time testing identifies timing vulnerabilities in cryptographic code where execution speed correlates with secret data. Developers use it when auditing crypto implementations - RSA, ECDH, AES, and post-quantum algorithms - to prevent timing attacks that extract private keys or encryption keys remotely. The workflow combines four tool categories: statistical testing (dudect) detects leakage via Welch's t-test, dynamic tracing (Timecop) pinpoints exact leak locations by tracking secret propagation, symbolic execution finds cache-timing attacks, and formal verification mathematically proves absence of leaks. Common vulnerabilities include secret-dependent branches, array lookups indexed by secrets, and variable-time division or shift operations. Integration into CI pipelines ensures continuous monitoring across compilers and architectures. Four tool categories address timing analysis: formal verification (proofs), symbolic execution (counterexamples), dynamic tracing (runtime location), and statistical testing (practical detection). Detects four critical vulnerability patterns: conditional branches on secrets, secret-indexed array access, variable-time division, variable-tim.

items.summary: The evm-token-decimals skill EVMチェーン全体でサイレントな小数点不一致バグを防ぐ。ランタイムでの小数点照会、チェーン対応キャッシング、ブリッジドトークンの精度ドリフト、ボット・ダッシュボード・DeFiツール向けの安全な正規化をカバーします。. サイレントな小数点不一致は、エラーを発生させることなく残高やUSD値が桁違いになる最も簡単な方法のひとつです。 - Python、TypeScript、またはSolidityでERC-20残高を読み取る場合 - オンチェーン残高から法定通貨の値を計算する場合 - 複数のEVMチェーン間でトークン量を比較する場合 - ブリッジされた資産を扱う場合 - ポートフォリオトラッカー、ボット、またはアグリゲーターを構築する場合 ステーブルコインが同じ小数点を使用していると仮定しないでください。ランタイムでdecimals()を照会し、(chain_id, token_address)でキャッシュし、値の計算には小数点安全な数学を使用します。 ```python from decimal import Decimal from web3 import Web3 python from decimal import Decimal from web3 import Web3 ERC20_ABI = [ {"name": "decimals", "type": "function", "inputs": [], "outputs": [{"type": "uint8"}], "stateMutability": "view"}, {"name": "balanceOf", "type": "function", "inputs": [{"name": "account", "type": "address"}], "outputs": [{"type": "uint256"}], "stateMutability": "view"}, ] def get_token_balance(w3: Web3, token_address: str, wallet: str) - Decimal: contract = w3.eth.contract( address=Web3.to_checksum_address(token_address), abi=ERC20_ABI, ) decimals = contract.functions.decimals().call() raw = contract.functions.balanceOf(Web3.to_checksum_address(wallet)).call() return Decimal(raw) / Decimal(10 decimals).

items.summary: PixiJS Scene Core Concepts is the shared mental model for PixiJS v8 display lists covering containers, leaves, transforms, render order, culling, render groups, masking, and destroy semantics. Every display object is a Container subclass; leaves such as Sprite, Graphics, Text, Mesh, and GifSprite must not hold children, while grouping belongs in Container or RenderLayer nodes. The renderer walks the tree each frame, composes local and world transforms, culls offscreen nodes, and draws siblings in array order with optional sortableChildren zIndex or RenderLayer decoupling. Render groups with isRenderGroup true move transform work to the GPU for large stable subtrees. Masking supports Graphics stencil, Sprite alpha, and ColorMask types. Visibility versus renderable flags split skip-render from keep-transform-update behavior for hit testing. Destroy with children true recursively tears down branches and optional texture cleanup. The skill maps each leaf type to dedicated pixijs-scene leaf skills and points to scene-management and masking references for deeper patterns.

items.summary: batch-processor is a Claude Office skill for high-volume document operations across PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and mixed file folders. A checkpoint-based BatchProcessor class persists processed state to JSON so long jobs can resume after interruption without reprocessing completed files. Example prompts cover mass PDF-to-Word conversion, folder-wide text extraction from images, batch rename and organize tasks, and mass header or footer updates across document sets. The skill integrates with the office-mcp server through the batch_convert tool and supports English and Chinese workflows. Installation expects python-docx, openpyxl, python-pptx, reportlab, and jinja2. Best practices emphasize tqdm feedback, checkpoint files for reliability, conservative worker limits, and failure logging for later review. Developers reach for it when repetitive document transforms must run across large directories without manual one-by-one handling.

items.name: contagious
items.author: wondelai
items.description: Analyze real-world viral products through the STEPPS framework and extract repeatable psychological triggers for their own launches.
items.summary: contagious applies Jonah Berger's STEPPS framework to design products, campaigns, and content for offline and online word-of-mouth. The core principle states virality is engineered: only seven percent of word-of-mouth happens online while ninety-three percent happens in offline conversations, so sharing psychology matters more than social mechanics alone. STEPPS covers Social Currency, Triggers, Emotion, Public visibility, Practical Value, and Stories, scored toward a ten-out-of-ten activation goal with explicit improvement notes. Social currency focuses on remarkability, game mechanics, and exclusivity without false scarcity. Triggers link products to frequent environmental cues because daily reminders outperform rare powerful ones. Emotion prioritizes high-arousal feelings such as awe, excitement, amusement, anger, or anxiety over low-arousal sadness or contentment. Public, practical value, and stories sections add observability, helpful pass-along utility, and narrative embedding patterns with ethical boundaries on manipulation. Developers invoke it for go viral requests, shareable features, referral design, organic growth planning, or STEPPS scoring of existing launches.

WebGL advanced modes require useBackBuffer true at app.init or they silently fall back.

items.description: Automatically detect threats, manage incidents, and maintain compliance across production systems.
items.summary: Security Monitoring automates threat detection, incident response, and compliance workflows using security-mcp tools siem_query, alert_create, incident_manage, and compliance_check. The architecture ingests firewall, endpoint, cloud, network, and application logs into a SIEM data lake, runs rule-based and ML anomaly detection with threat intelligence correlation, then triggers alerting, ticketing, and automated containment. Detection rules cover brute-force login, impossible travel, large data egress, known malware hashes, lateral movement chains, and privilege escalation sequences with severity-tuned response times. Alert configuration defines critical fifteen-minute pager responses, deduplication windows, and Slack or email notification channels. Incident workflows progress through triage, containment, investigation, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review with playbook automation for ransomware and phishing scenarios including endpoint isolation, account disable, and evidence preservation. Compliance monitoring ties into related devops-automation and log-analysis skills for holistic security operations.
highlights: SIEM architecture from multi-source log ingestion through detection engine to automated response actions.
Detection rules for brute force, impossible travel, data exfiltration, malware hashes, and lateral movement correlation.
Alert severity tiers with response SLAs, deduplication, and Slack, email, or PagerDuty notifications.
Incident workflow from triage through containment, investigation, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review.
Playbook automation for ransomware and phishing with isolate, disable account, and preserve evidence steps.

Best practices stress null edge cases, exact violation counts, stateless custom validators, and keeping validation tests out of controller integration layers. Reference files document custom validators and advanced validation group patterns. The skill explicitly targets fast unit tests without Spring Boot context or database dependencies.

items.name: eval-driven-dev
items.author: github
items.description: Deeply understand a codebase's real-world purpose, users, and capabilities before defining any evaluations, traces, or tests.
items.summary: eval-driven-dev implements an automated evaluation pipeline for Python LLM applications using pixie-qa and pixie test. Invoke it when users ask to add evals, benchmark LLM behavior, set up QA, or fix wrong outputs in Python projects that call real models. The workflow runs six sequential steps: understand the app and define eval criteria, instrument data boundaries with wrap, implement a Runnable in pixie_qa/run_app.py, define evaluators, build a golden dataset, run pixie test, and analyze outcomes into action plans. Critical rules forbid mocking the LLM in eval Runnable code because that makes scores tautological; external data sources are injected via instrumentations while app routing and prompt assembly run for real. Setup activates a virtual environment, runs resources/setup.sh to install pixie-qa, pixie init, and pixie start for the results web UI. Deliverables include pixie_qa markdown context files, reference-trace.jsonl, evaluator mapping, dataset JSON, scored test results, and per-dataset analysis with action-plan summaries. Compatibility requires Python 3.10 plus pixie-qa version 0.8.4 or newer.
highlights: Six-step pixie-qa workflow from project analysis through pixie test execution and outcome analysis.
Requires real LLM calls in the Runnable; forbids mocking or stubbing the model in eval harness code.

Assets.load on a GIF returns GifSource, not Texture, so wrap with GifSprite instead of Sprite. Constructor options include autoPlay, loop, animationSpeed, autoUpdate, fps fallback, and onComplete, onLoop, onFrameChange callbacks. GifSprite is a leaf display object; group multiple instances in a Container. Share one GifSource across sprites with independent playback or clone settings. Manual update mode disconnects from Ticker.shared when autoUpdate is false. For performance-critical multi-frame animation prefer AnimatedSprite with a spritesheet atlas. items.description: Stop Claude from guessing and force concrete investigation before any file edit or bash command.
items.summary: gateguard is a PreToolUse hook that forces investigation before file edits instead of unreliable LLM self-evaluation. The three-stage gate denies the first Edit, Write, or destructive Bash attempt, forces the model to gather concrete facts, then allows retry after facts are presented. Edit and MultiEdit gates require listing all importers, affected public symbols, data schema fields and date formats with redacted values, and quoting the user instruction verbatim. Write gates demand caller file and line references, Glob confirmation no duplicate exists, and the same data schema check. Destructive Bash gates trigger on rm -rf, git reset --hard, git push --force, and drop table with rollback procedures required. Routine Bash gates once per session ask for the current request and command purpose. Documented A/B tests show gated agents averaging 9.0 versus 6.75 ungated on analytics and webhook validator tasks. Enable via scripts/hooks/gateguard-fact-force.js in hooks.json or pip install gateguard-ai with .gateguard.yml ignore paths. ECC_GATEGUARD=off disables during setup. Complements safety-guard runtime checks and post-edit code-reviewer skill.
highlights: Three-stage gate: deny first edit, force fact gathering, allow retry after investigation.

items.summary: Slack Messaging Best Practices teaches agents to compose effective Slack messages using mrkdwn, which differs from standard Markdown. Formatting rules cover bold with single asterisks, italic with underscores, strikethrough with tildes, inline and block code with backticks, quotes with angle brackets, and links as url|display text in angle brackets. Common mistakes to avoid include double-asterisk bold, Markdown headers, bracket-paren links, and horizontal rules that Slack does not render. Message structure guidance says lead with the point in the first line, keep messages to one to three short paragraphs, use line breaks generously, convert three or more items into bullet lists, and bold names, dates, deadlines, and action items. Thread etiquette recommends replying in threads for specific messages, using reply_broadcast only when everyone needs the reply, posting new topics in the channel, and continuing existing conversations in the original thread. Tone should match the channel, with emoji reactions suggested for simple acknowledgments when MCP tools cannot add reactions directly.

items.summary: Swift Concurrency helps developers review, fix, and write concurrent Swift code targeting Swift 6.3+ with actor isolation, Sendable safety, and structured concurrency patterns. The triage workflow captures compiler diagnostics, concurrency settings including Approachable Concurrency and Default MainActor isolation, and whether code is UI-bound before applying the smallest safe fix. Swift 6.2 changes cover SE-0466 default MainActor isolation, SE-0461 nonisolated(nonsending), @concurrent for background work, SE-0472 Task.immediate, and SE-0475 Observations for @Observable types. Actor rules require protecting mutable shared state, using @MainActor for UI code, and avoiding manual locks inside actors. Sendable rules favor immutable value types, document @unchecked Sendable as last resort, and use sending parameters for cross-isolation callbacks. Structured concurrency patterns include async let, TaskGroup, task cancellation with .task in SwiftUI, and actor reentrancy awareness across await points. Common mistakes span blocking MainActor, unnecessary actors, Task.detached overuse, semaphores in async code, and GCD APIs. A review checklist confirms isolation, cancellation, and @concurr.

items.name: gh-address-comments
items.author: openai
items.description: Systematically address GitHub PR review comments using the gh CLI without leaving the coding environment.
items.summary: GH Address Comments is an OpenAI agent skill for triaging GitHub pull request feedback on the branch you have checked out. It starts by verifying gh authentication with gh auth status under escalated permissions, prompting login if needed. Step one runs scripts/fetch_comments.py to list comments and review threads on the open PR. Step two numbers every thread, summarizes what fixing each item would require, and asks the user which numbered comments to address. Step three applies code fixes only for the selected items. All gh commands need elevated network access, and auth or rate-limit failures should prompt re-login before retry. Unlike autonomous babysit loops, this skill emphasizes human selection of which review notes to tackle rather than continuous polling. It fits workflows where a PR already has open feedback and the developer wants a structured pass to resolve chosen comments before pushing updates.
highlights: Verifies gh auth status with escalated permissions before any PR comment fetch.
Runs scripts/fetch_comments.py to print PR comments and review threads.

items.description: Connect Claude directly to a local DeerFlow LangGraph instance for reliable streaming responses and threaded conversations.
items.summary: Claude to DeerFlow is an integration skill for calling a running DeerFlow AI agent platform over HTTP. DeerFlow sits behind an Nginx proxy with a Gateway API for models, skills, memory, and uploads and a LangGraph-compatible API for threads and streaming runs. Environment variables DEERFLOW_URL, DEERFLOW_GATEWAY_URL, and DEERFLOW_LANGGRAPH_URL must be resolved before any curl call, defaulting to localhost port 2026. Primary flow creates a thread, then POSTs a streaming run with assistant_id lead_agent, human messages, stream_mode values and messages-tuple, and context flags for thinking, plan mode, and subagents. items.summary: Medusa Storefront Development is the required skill for any storefront task involving custom API routes, SDK integration, React Query patterns, mutations, and cache invalidation when building on Medusa. Critical rules mandate always using the Medusa JS SDK instead of raw fetch because publishable API keys and auth headers are injected automatically. Built-in endpoints should use sdk.store and sdk.admin methods, while custom routes use sdk.client.fetch with plain object bodies never wrapped in JSON.stringify. React Query guidance covers useQuery for GET, useMutation for POST and DELETE, hierarchical query keys, invalidation on success, and handling isLoading, isPending, and isError states. A critical display rule states Medusa prices are stored as-is so 49.99 displays directly without dividing by 100. The skill requires loading references/frontend-integration.md before implementation and pairs with building-with-medusa for backend module, workflow, and API route work. Common mistakes checklist flags fetch usage, wrong SDK methods, missing invalidation, flat query keys, and price division errors.

items.summary: inngest-durable-functions is an agent skill for Inngest durable execution in TypeScript covering function creation, triggers, step memoization, idempotency, cancellation, error handling, and observability. The core rule places all non-deterministic code inside step.run because each step re-runs the function from the start while completed steps are memoized. Documented limits are 1,000 steps per function, 4MB per step return, 32MB combined state, and roughly 50-100ms overhead per step HTTP request. createFunction configures unique ids, event triggers with optional if filters, cron schedules with timezones, retries, and concurrency. Idempotency covers producer-side inngest.send custom ids and consumer-side idempotency keys on event fields. Cancellation patterns use cancelOn event matching and timeout cancellation. step.invoke composes smaller functions when limits are hit. Always wrap API calls, database IO, and file operations in steps; keep pure calculations outside. Developers reach for it when webhook handlers drop events, cron jobs are flaky, background jobs fail mid-execution, or workflows must resume after infrastructure crashes with automatic retries.
highlights: Non-deterministic code must live inside step.run due to memoized re-execution model.
Limits: 1,000 steps, 4MB per step, 32MB combined state per function run.

items.description: Implement reliable, retry-safe delays, waits, parallel steps, and external event handling inside durable Inngest workflows.
items.summary: The inngest-steps skill covers Inngest step methods for building durable workflows where each step is a separate HTTP request with independent retries. Critical rule: each step re-runs the function from the beginning, so all non-deterministic code must live inside steps, never outside. Documented methods include step.run for retriable work, step.sleep and step.sleepUntil for delays, step.waitForEvent for event matching with timeouts, step.waitForSignal for one-to-one signals, step.sendEvent for fan-out, and step.invoke for calling other functions with typed results. Limits are 1,000 steps and 4MB total step data per function. waitForEvent only catches events sent after the step executes and requires null checks on timeout. waitForSignal uses onConflict replace or fail for pending signals. invoke requires imported function references in v4, not string IDs. Patterns cover loops reusing step IDs with automatic counters and parallel step execution. TypeScript focus is explicit with pointers to Python and Go documentation. Use cases include cart abandonment delays, human approval gates, webhook polling, memoizing expensive operations, and parallel async work inside workflows.
highlights: Covers step.run, step.sleep, step.sleepUntil, step.waitForEvent, step.waitForSignal, step.sendEvent, step.invoke.

items.summary: background-processing covers registering, scheduling, and executing background work on iOS with BackgroundTasks, background URLSession, and silent push. UIBackgroundModes fetch and processing enable BGAppRefreshTask and BGProcessingTask respectively. Handlers register before app launch completes in AppDelegate or SwiftUI App.init. BGProcessingTask supports longer maintenance when idle and optionally on external power. BGContinuedProcessingTask on iOS 26+ continues foreground-started exports with ProgressReporting and Live Activity updates. Background URLSession downloads use delegate callbacks and store completion handlers for relaunch. Silent push requires content-available 1 and apns-push-type background with priority 5. Common mistakes include missing plist identifiers, skipping setTaskCompleted, scheduling refreshes too frequently, and a review checklist for simulated launches and incremental cancellation-safe work.

Bidding trees cover Google Maximize Clicks to Target ROAS progression, Meta CBO versus ABO, LinkedIn manual CPC, and TikTok fifty-times CPA learning thresholds. Scaling green lights require two weeks below-target CPA, fifty weekly conversions, stable CTR, and no creative fatigue. Kill framework pauses CPA above three times target, zero conversions after sufficient spend, and creatives with CTR below half the benchmark. Deliverables include BUDGET-STRATEGY-REPORT.md, scale and kill lists, MER analysis, and platform bidding recommendations.
